title: Cardinal Luigi d'Este's cipher, 1584-85: BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 (April 1584) and four passages of Colbert 338 (pp. 513, 517-518 and 523), all read in part with Tomokiyo's key (strict: f. 271 85.0%, p. 517 87.9%, p. 518 80.6%, p. 513 83.0%, p. 523 73.0%)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's d'Este table applied to Colbert 338; shape names fixed on glossed pages 435-438, 453-454, 504.
Five tests against the volume's contemporary glosses (V1-V5): best V2 p. 504, 0.777 characters vs 0.332 (thresholds 0.85/0.75); V4 and V5 not admissible (glosses not literal).
Probable words from a list fixed in advance placed on the training pages only: alpha with a descending tail = f; key K-C01 frozen.
One measurement on held-out p. 523: M5 0.457 vs 0.078 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (gap 0.379); thresholds >= 0.60 and >= +0.30.
Read by sense after a blind shape sheet of 14 questions: 200 words, 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved (88.5%).
Cryptiana re-read; Favalli 2024 read in full; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435) not readable; web searches for an edition of fr. 16041-16042 or of this advice: nothing.
Probable words placed on pages already seen only (pp. 436-438, 453-454, 504, 523): sig = m, A = [fait], Venus sign = [faire], newt = nn; key K-C02 frozen and hashed.
One pre-registered measurement on held-out p. 517 lines 4-29 (979 signs): M5 0.509 vs 0.067 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (gap 0.442); thresholds >= 0.45 and >= +0.30 fixed before.
p. 517 read by sense: 231 words, 201 certain, 22 probable, 3 restored, 5 unresolved (96.5%).

Integration check (PR #546): own decoder from key-p517.tsv equals decryption-p517.txt on all 29 lines; M5 re-implemented from validation.txt gives 0.509 against best control 0.068 (median 0.025) on lines 4-29; about 110 signs of lines 1, 2 and 20 agree with the Gallica image (IIIF f272). Frozen files not in the PR (key-p517.tsv is a later copy: 98ef85f6 vs frozen aa7d73db), order of events by the contributor's record. Strict recount by the README bar: p. 517 201/231 = 87.0%, p. 523 146/200 = 73.0% (probable, restored and unresolved words are holes); contributor's 96.5% and 88.5% kept as theirs. Both pages read in part.

Values for new and contradicted shapes taken from p. 517 (after its measurement) and p. 518 (training page): Venus sign = o, barred dumbbell = null, y = [Espagne], four new shapes; key K-C03 frozen and hashed with a pre-registration naming p. 513 as held-out block.
Pre-registered test on p. 513 not run: the frozen block has 208 signs, under the 300 required by the pre-registration; K-C03 stays unvalidated and its values are given as probable.

p. 518 read by sense with K-C02 and the probable values: 108 words, 87 certain, 16 probable, 1 restored, 4 unresolved (95.4%, after a blind shape sheet of 14 Nov 2026; 94.4% before); the letter pp. 517-518 together 326/339 = 96.2%.
p. 513 cipher block read: 47 words, 38 certain, 5 probable, 4 unresolved (91.5%); checked against the contemporary margin decipherment, which agrees and gives 'Espaigne' for the code word y.

K-C03.1 re-tested once on a new document, BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 (677 signs, pre-registered, frozen transcription): M5 0.451 vs 0.077 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (gap 0.374); thresholds 0.45 and +0.30: validated at the bar (0.451 against 0.45, a margin of 0.001).
fr. 16041 f. 271 read by sense: 160 words, 135 certain, 17 probable, 3 restored, 5 unresolved (95.0%); g8 = m and new3 = u learned on the page.

Integration check of PR #557: own decoders from key-p517.tsv (pp. 518, 513) and key-f16041-271.tsv (f. 271) equal the committed decryptions on every line (490, 208 and 677 signs); M5 re-implemented on f. 271: 0.451 (fr), 0.374 (it), best shuffled 0.08-0.11; Gallica images (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF) compared: about 125 signs of p. 518 (L1, L2, L8, L9), 60 of p. 513 (L8, L9, with the code word y in place) and 80 of f. 271 (L1, L2, L10) agree; the p. 513 margin reads '...oy qu'en Espaig[ne] / de Longlée / ...dvise qu'ilz font / ...tiques si l'eglise / ...geoit de pasteur / ...tiffiant leurs / ...saings et / ...oiblissant ceulx / ...aultres, et / ...a esté envoyé / ordre exprès / ...pour ce que / ...chose tant / ...portant pour / ...ruice du Roy', as the reading. Strict recount with y attested: p. 517 203/231, p. 513 39/47, f. 271 136/160; p. 518 87/108 unchanged.

A contemporary clear copy of the whole letter pp. 517-518, postscript included (in French), is on p. 515 (Gallica view 271, right page), headed 'Ce memoire doit suivre apres la letre de Cardinal de Pellevé qui est cy dessus pag. 425'; found at the integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026), after the transcription, the test and the reading; not used by the reading. It reads 'la court de Savoye', 'du Roy d'Espaigne', 'escript en Espaigne'. Spot checks against the reading of p. 518: 'suivant' where the cipher gives 'suldant', 'fermer' before 'mes letres', 'm'a donné de tant plus grand suspect' (cipher 'docue de tant'), 'en tel pays' at the end, '[Sa] Saincteté' as restored. Not yet compared word by word; not used for any count except to attest y.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Satoshi Tomokiyo's published d'Este table, adjusted on glossed and already-read pages of the same volume (keys K-C01, K-C02); K-C02 passed a pre-registered held-out test on p. 517 (bar 0.45, lowered from 0.60 before the test, by the contributor's record); two signs (Venus sign, barred dumbbell) stay open, and the code word y, a sense-only value at first, is attested as Espagne by the p. 513 margin and the p. 515 clear copy since the check of PR #557. pp. 518 and 513 (after PR #546) read with K-C02 unchanged plus probable values for new shapes (key-p518-513.tsv); the pre-registered test of these values (K-C03) could not run (p. 513 too short). K-C03.1 (K-C03 + one clerical fix) then passed a pre-registered test on a new document, BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 (M5 0.451 vs 0.077, bar 0.45: passed by 0.001 only, 14 Nov 2026). Integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026): M5 0.451 on f. 271 re-implemented and reproduced (best control 0.08-0.11 across shuffling seeds, so the gap holds); the frozen files of the three pre-registrations are not in the repository, so the order of events is by the contributor's record. A contemporary clear copy of the letter pp. 517-518 was found on p. 515 at that check; it was not used by the reading and has not yet been compared word by word.
outcome.fraction_read_source: README read bar applied strictly, per page, never pooled (certain words only; probable, restored and unresolved words are holes). fraction_read is p. 523, the page first written up: 146/200 = 73.0%. Other pages: p. 517 203/231 = 87.9% (201/231 = 87.0% at the check of 13 Nov; the two 'Espagne' words count as sure since the check of PR #557, 14 Nov 2026, y being attested at pp. 513 and 515), p. 518 87/108 = 80.6%, p. 513 39/47 = 83.0%, BnF fr. 16041 f. 271 136/160 = 85.0%. The contributor's figures (certain + probable): p. 523 177/200 = 88.5%, p. 517 223/231 = 96.5%, p. 518 103/108 = 95.4% (letter pp. 517-518 326/339 = 96.2%), p. 513 43/47 = 91.5%, f. 271 152/160 = 95.0%.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py). p. 523 (5 Nov, key K-C01): M5 0.457 vs 0.078, partial (thresholds 0.60 / +0.30). p. 517 lines 4-29 (13 Nov, key K-C02, thresholds 0.45 / +0.30 fixed before from the clear texts of the volume): M5 0.509 vs 0.067, validated. Integration check (13 Nov 2026): no M5 script in the PR; an own re-implementation from the description gives M5 0.509, best control 0.068, median 0.025 on p. 517 lines 4-29 (code words spelled out). The p. 517 bar (0.45) was lowered from p. 523's 0.60 before the test, by the contributor's record; the frozen pre-registration, key file and block are not in the repository (the committed key-p517.tsv is a later copy: it hashes to 98ef85f6, the frozen value is aa7d73db). fr. 16041 f. 271 (14 Nov 2026, after PR #546, key K-C03.1, same thresholds, French/Italian lexicons): M5 0.451 vs 0.077, validated at the bar (0.451 against 0.45: a margin of 0.001). Integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026): own M5 implementation (fr and it lexicons, frequency >= 5, 5+ letters, separators removed, code words spelled out) gives 0.451 (fr) and 0.374 (it) on the frozen f. 271 transcription, as stated; best of 200 shuffled keys 0.110 with seed 271 in our shuffling (0.080-0.106 with other seeds; contributor 0.077), so the gap stays above 0.30. PREREG-KC03, PREREG-KC03b, AVENANT-1, the frozen K-C03/K-C03.1 key files, the frozen block and mlex2.py are not in the repository: the committed key-f16041-271.tsv and transcription-f16041-271.txt carry headers and do not hash to the stated values, so the pre-registration is by the contributor's record. The pass is at the bar by 0.001.

texts.label: BnF fr. 16041 f. 271, whole page in cipher (letter of Luigi d'Este to Villeroy, April 1584)
texts.summary: Luigi d'Este writes that, by common report, the Pope cannot last long, falling back so often into his illnesses; he is in the country for eight days, after which d'Este will speak to him 'as of himself', as Villeroy's letter asks, about the Duke of Montmorency and the King's gentleness towards him, arguing that the duke would not defy the King unless backed by someone greater (Spain is named in line 1), and that the Pope's predecessors were wont to ...

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 14 Nov 2026 by one AI reader after the measurement: 135 certain, 17 probable, 3 restored, 5 unresolved of 160 words (95.0%, at the bar); five arbitration choices corrected while reading (listed); each probable word justified in reading-f16041-271.md. No palaeographer checked the page.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share (README read bar): 136 certain of 160 words = 85.0%; the 16 probable, 3 restored ([lettre], [Sa], [sera]) and 5 unresolved words are holes. The contributor's strict figure was 135/160 = 84.4% with 'd'Espagne' (code word y) probable; at the integration check of PR #557 it counts as sure (y attested at Colbert 338 pp. 513 and 515). The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 152/160 = 95.0%.

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 517, whole page in cipher
texts.summary: The writer hears that the pope was told, from the court of ‹T…› (Savoy in the clear copy on p. 515), that 'this duke' had letters from the King of Spain urging him to make war on the King and protect Marshal de Montmorency; he doubts it, explains Montmorency's fears of Joyeuse around Clermont-de-Lodève and his letters to Spain, and hopes Poigny's mission has calmed him, as the levy of 4,000 foot in the State of Milan has melted away.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 13 Nov 2026 by one AI reader: 201 certain, 22 probable, 3 restored, 5 unresolved of 231 words (96.5%), each probable word justified in reading-p517.md; the code word y restored as Spain by sense only. No palaeographer checked the page.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share (README read bar): 203 certain of 231 words = 87.9%; the 22 probable, 1 restored (que) and 5 unresolved words are holes. Recounted at the integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026): the code word y is now attested as Espagne by two contemporary witnesses (the margin decipherment of p. 513 and the clear copy of this letter on p. 515), so the two 'Espagne' words, restored by sense at the check of 13 Nov (201/231 = 87.0%), count as sure. The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 223/231 = 96.5% ('read').

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 518, lines 1-16 in cipher (end of the letter of p. 517)
texts.summary: End of the p. 517 letter: the writer asks that the news be referred to His Majesty and doubts it bodes well for the pacification with Montmorency; going to his audience before closing his letters, he discussed Languedoc with the Pope, who ordered him to do all he can so that the King comes to terms with Marshal de Montmorency to calm the troubles.

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 513, cipher block of the letter of 2 January 1585
texts.summary: Luigi d'Este reports that, according to the sieur de Longlée, in Spain they are scheming in case the Church changes its shepherd (the pope dies), strengthening their designs and weakening those of others, and that express orders have been sent to Rome; a matter of great importance for the King's service. Already deciphered in the margin at the time.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 13 Nov 2026 by one AI reader: 38 certain, 5 probable, 4 unresolved of 47 words (91.5%); the contemporary margin decipherment, looked at after the transcription was frozen, agrees word for word where legible.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share (README read bar): 39 certain of 47 words = 83.0%; the 4 probable and 4 unresolved words are holes. The contributor counted 'Espagne' (code word y) as probable (38/47 = 80.9% strict); at the integration check of PR #557 it counts as sure, the value being attested by the margin decipherment of this page and by the clear copy on p. 515. The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 43/47 = 91.5%.

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 523, whole page in cipher
texts.summary: A prince (name in a code word, not read) had the pope asked for the title of king and was refused; he turned to the emperor; the writer was told the emperor alone gave Cosimo of Florence his grand-ducal title; he asks that the King be told and that his source among the pope's people stay secret.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026 by one AI reader; Brice Dudout answered the shape sheet only. The decryption construes as French sentences with gaps: 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved of 200 words (88.5%), so read in part.

prior.where: The key: S. Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, 'Cardinal d'Este's Cipher (1584-1586)' (henryiii.htm), built on BnF fr. 16041-16042; Colbert 338 not cited, no letter edited. The text of p. 523: no edition found; Favalli, CHMO 49/2 (2024), read, covers 1569-1580 and does not mention it; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435, 1559-1580) not read in full. Catalogue 1572 open on origin/main (GitHub API, e2315f8a, 5 Nov 2026). p. 517 (13 Nov 2026): no edition found; one web search on Poigny / Montmorency / Joyeuse / Clermont-de-Lodève 1584 found nothing printing this advice. pp. 513 and 518 (13 Nov 2026): p. 513's cipher block is deciphered in the margin by a contemporary hand (our reading agrees); no edition of either page found (three web searches: Luigi d'Este's letters to Henri III / Villeroy, Longlée, Desjardins' Négociations avec la Toscane - its tome IV prints the Florentine envoys' dispatches, not d'Este's French letters; not checked page by page). fr. 16041 f. 271 (14 Nov 2026): Tomokiyo cites only ff. 259 and 264 of fr. 16041 and prints no decipherment; nothing on fr. 16041-16042 in this repository; one web search on this letter (Montmorency, the pope's illness, April 1584) found no edition; three short contemporary interlinear glosses on the page. Contemporary decipherments in the same volume, Colbert 338: the margin of p. 513 (its own cipher block) and p. 515, a contemporary clear copy of the whole letter pp. 517-518, found at the integration check of PR #557 (14 Nov 2026), after the reading; nothing in the contributor's files mentions p. 515, and it was used only to attest y.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target, set the rules (protocols and amendments hashed before each computation, one measurement on a held-out page, thresholds fixed in advance) and answered the blind shape sheet (shapes only). AI agents transcribed, applied and adjusted the key, measured, read and wrote up. No palaeographer checked the page.
